The Torah, the first five books of the Jewish Bible (also known as the Pentateuch in the Christian Bible): Bereshit (Genesis), Shemot (Exodus), Vayikra (Leviticus), Bamidbar (Numbers) and Devarim (Deuteronomy). These books contain the early history, mythology, laws and traditions of the Jewish people. Traditionally attributed to Moses ~1300 BCE, most biblical scholars now believe that the books were written between ~600-400 BCE.
